question: Verify ligand identity and assay integrity
hypothesis: Reference graphs, identities and signals must be correct before testing mechanism.
comparison: Use authentic 9CH TH5427; 9/10/11; provisional 13; 12 or 15; vehicle. Confirm LC-MS/NMR identity and purity, soluble/free concentration and stability.
controls: No-enzyme wells; AMP or ATP standard added to detection chemistry; compound-only optical/luminescence blanks; DMSO matching; concentration-dependent precipitation/aggregation checks.
readout: Purity, identity, solubility; detection signal at fixed product.
falsifier_or_interpretation: Apparent inhibition reproduced without enzyme, or disappears in direct product detection, refutes a catalytic-inhibition interpretation.
gate_or_limit: All compounds before biochemical or cell experiments.
evidence_status: Design recommendation; chemical graph and parent compounds verified in P/B/CCD.

question: Remeasure two-target catalytic and binding selectivity
hypothesis: Existing N1 substituents and compound 13 provide differential NUDT5/NUDT14 starting points.
comparison: Recombinant human NUDT5 and NUDT14; direct ADPr-to-AMP LC-MS/HPLC initial rates over substrate and inhibitor ranges; SPR as orthogonal binding. Independent protein preparations and biological repeats; fit CIs.
controls: Establish each enzyme Km and linear time range; hold free Mg, solvent and temperature constant; examine fixed substrate and matched S/Km comparisons; detergent and protein-concentration sensitivity. Use no-enzyme/validated stopped reactions for 0% signal, not assumed TH5427 inhibition of NUDT14.
readout: Initial-rate concentration responses and direct KD; uncertainty on cross-target selectivity.
falsifier_or_interpretation: Loss of bias in direct assays defeats reliance on published endpoint IC50 ratios. Binding without rate inhibition is not evidence of catalytic blockade.
gate_or_limit: E1; do not treat endpoint ratios as intrinsic affinity selectivity.
evidence_status: B Methods used 1 nM enzyme, 10 uM ADPr, 1 mM MgCl2, but 20 min versus 1 h; proposed assay is a new test.

question: Disentangle hydrolysis from ATP production
hypothesis: A compound affecting ADPr hydrolysis may not inhibit the ATP-producing state to the same extent.
comparison: Separately measure NUDT5 products from ADPr plus PPi by validated direct nucleotide analysis; reproduce the PARG/PAR-coupled system only as an additional arm.
controls: No enzyme; no PPi; known ATP spike; enzyme activity control; no PARG control for coupled arm; exclude direct PARG inhibition.
readout: Resolved AMP and ATP product formation, preferably isotope-traced where needed to separate background.
falsifier_or_interpretation: Preserved ATP production despite hydrolysis inhibition falsifies the inference that the hydrolysis assay predicts ATP-synthesis blockade.
gate_or_limit: E1-E2; analytical separation and enzyme activity validated.
evidence_status: P Fig.4a verifies the published coupled system; proposed direct-product comparison is not a result.

question: Falsify Arg51-dependent ligand recognition
hypothesis: TH5427 affinity depends more strongly on NUDT5 Arg51 than compound 9 affinity does.
comparison: Proposed NUDT5 WT/R51K/R51A proteins; test TH5427 and 9 direct binding. Only subsequently design a chemically matched acceptor-present/absent pair.
controls: Verify folding, thermal behavior, soluble abundance and dimer by SEC-MALS or equivalent; characterize substrate kinetics; do not call these catalytic-dead or resistance alleles.
readout: Change in direct affinity per ligand with uncertainty; catalytic baseline as quality control.
falsifier_or_interpretation: Similar affinity penalties undermine differential dependence. Unfolding, loss of dimer or globally lost function makes the perturbation uninterpretable, not supportive.
gate_or_limit: Use full biological dimer; check local density before atom-level design; no docking required.
evidence_status: P/B published recognition assignments; mutant results and new-ligand selectivity are hypotheses.

question: Establish dose-dependent cellular target coverage
hypothesis: Biochemical differences translate to a usable cellular window.
comparison: Dose/time NUDT5 NanoBRET or endogenous engagement and NUDT14 HiBiT-CETSA plus an orthogonal endogenous method where feasible; assess BTK in the intended cell model.
controls: Reporter-only and cell-free interference; total tagged/endogenous protein; viability; intracellular exposure; unheated abundance controls for CETSA; counterscreen BTK comparator against both NUDIX enzymes.
readout: Target engagement versus concentration, free exposure and protein abundance.
falsifier_or_interpretation: No distinct target-coverage window blocks single-target chemical attribution; negative CETSA alone cannot establish absence of binding.
gate_or_limit: E1-E2; measure in intended cell context, not only HEK293 transfectants.
evidence_status: B Fig.5: 9 NUDT5 EC50 1.08 uM, BTK 0.377 uM; NUDT14 thermal stabilization measured at 30 uM.

question: Test the acute hormone response
hypothesis: NUDT5 catalytic inhibition precedes and explains the early hormone-response defect without protein loss.
comparison: Hormone-starved T47D +/- R5020; TH5427 and 9 at matched measured NUDT5 coverage. Proposed early 15-120 min time course, then transcription and later EdU/cell counts.
controls: Vehicle +/- hormone; nuclear and cytosolic ATP readouts; direct reporter inhibition and pH controls; general toxicity; total/nuclear target protein abundance at each time.
readout: Early nuclear ATP dynamics, hormone-responsive transcription, later proliferation by non-ATP-dependent readout.
falsifier_or_interpretation: A reporter-only effect or generalized ATP/viability collapse refutes a specific nuclear mechanism. Lack of acute effect at verified coverage weakens catalytic sufficiency.
gate_or_limit: E5; concentration selection is exposure-driven, not copied from literature.
evidence_status: P Fig.4 establishes hormone-dependent T47D context; proposed timeline/causal comparisons remain untested.

question: Separate NUDT14 contribution from other off-target effects
hypothesis: Any additional effect of dual inhibitor 9 depends on NUDT14.
comparison: Factorial NUDT5 depletion, NUDT14 depletion, double depletion and nontargeting control crossed with vehicle/TH5427/9; independent genetic reagents; near-endogenous WT rescue for each target. Add 13 only after E5 validates its window.
controls: Verify depletion and rescue; matched dynamic range and target coverage; avoid basal floor/ceiling effects; counterscreen plausible BTK contributions.
readout: Change in additional 9 effect with NUDT14 depletion and restoration by NUDT14 rescue.
falsifier_or_interpretation: Persistence after verified double depletion with adequate dynamic range points to other targets/artifacts; nonadditivity alone is not epistasis proof.
gate_or_limit: E5-E6; genetic adaptation/viability and incomplete depletion assessed.
evidence_status: Proposed causal design, not established by either paper.

question: Separate catalytic activity from protein-presence functions
hypothesis: A protein-loss phenotype can differ from an acute catalytic-inhibition phenotype.
comparison: Inducible NUDT5 depletion plus near-endogenous WT versus independently validated catalytically inactive NUDT5 rescue; compare acute inhibitor and delayed depletion endpoints.
controls: Inactive construct must retain folding, dimerization, localization and comparable abundance; verify WT rescue works; characterize both hydrolysis and ATP-production activity; total/nuclear protein time courses.
readout: WT versus inactive rescue of ATP/transcription/proliferation; phenotype timing relative to target protein abundance.
falsifier_or_interpretation: WT-only rescue supports catalysis. Rescue by inactive protein supports a noncatalytic role. Failed or partial rescue without construct validity remains inconclusive; inhibitor effect before loss is not alone proof.
gate_or_limit: Catalytic-dead allele must be experimentally validated; no specific validated allele identified here.
evidence_status: Proposed falsification plan; no claim that cited papers demonstrate drug-induced NUDT5 degradation.
